e\varnothing. \] The weak certificate uses exactly fifty-six scalar lift variables, eight \(3	imes3\) PSD blocks, and eight augmented \(4	imes4\) PSD blocks; the strict certificate uses sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6	imes6\) common-Hankel-range blocks. In the forward direction, each legal \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_v(c)\) is mapped to the eight joint response measures \(d

u_s\) and its five quartic moments. In the reverse direction, every feasible lift yields positive-half-line representing measures \((ho_s)_{s\in S}\); after setting \(d
u_s=D_c dho_s\), the construction \(\mu=\sum_{s\in S}
u_s\) and the Radon--Nikodym reconstructions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}response	ext{-}measure	ext{-}equivalence}\) produce one unconditional probability law together with legal initial and feedback kernels that generate exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\). For \(v=+\), the common-Hankel-range blocks yield representing measures on one positive-node set with strictly positive type weights, so the reconstructed \(h_x\) and \(g_{xy}\) satisfy the strict legal class. These equivalences are a strict finite-dimensional tightening of the continuous-support program in Proposition 1 of Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham while describing the same weak and strict legal model fibers.
body.justification: The two-sided theorem removes both the support-grid approximation and the latent-law quantifier while preserving the independently defined weak and strict causal fibers.
body.gap: The closest feedback program remains infinite-dimensional, and the closest truncated-Stieltjes analysis does not provide the separate unrestricted-feedback kernel or the common-support strict-positivity reconstruction.
body.consumer: The exact finite cone supplies sharp, grid-free slope--APE feasibility and endpoint calculations for the two-wave predetermined-children labor-participation design.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\).  The restriction \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}observed\text{-}cells}\) places \(P\) in the stated full positive-law domain.  Every division or change of measure below instead uses the explicitly stated facts \(c>0\), \(u>0\), and Radon--Nikodym domination.

Start with a legal weak model.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\), it yields eight nonnegative joint response measures \(\nu_s\) whose sum is one probability measure.  Since
\[
 D_c(u)=(1+u)^2(1+cu)^2>0
 \quad(c>0, u>0),
\]
define \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\).  For each \(0\le k\le4\), the function \(u^k/D_c(u)\) is bounded on \((0,\infty)\): it has a finite limit as \(u\downarrow0\), and it is of order \(u^{k-4}\) as \(u\to\infty\).  Thus all five moments \(m_{s,k}\) are finite.  Direct cancellation using the definition of \(p\) gives
\[
 D_c(u)p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)
 =c^{xy+zw}u^{y+w}(1+u)^{x+z}(1+cu)^{2-x-z}
 =A_{xz,yw}(u), \tag{5}
\]
and the definition of the APE integrand gives
\[
 D_c(u)\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}
 =(c-1)u(1+u)(1+cu)=N_c(u). \tag{6}
\]
The polynomials in (5)--(6) have degree at most four.  Hence the response-measure equations are exactly
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}L_{m_{(x,r)}}(A_{xz,yw}),
 \qquad
 \Delta=\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(N_c). \tag{7}
\]
For every type, \(\mathrm{lem{:}open\text{-}stieltjes\text{-}quartic}\) supplies \(a_s,b_s\) such that \(H_s\succeq0\) and \(K_s\succeq0\).  Equations (7) and \(\mathrm{def{:}weak\text{-}lift}\) prove \(\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing\).

Suppose now that the original model is strict.  For every \(s=(x,r_0,r_1)\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}initial}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}feedback}\) imply
\[
 h_x(u)g_{x0}(r_0,u)g_{x1}(r_1,u)>0
 \quad\text{for }\mu\text{-almost every }u.
\]
Consequently every \(\nu_s\), and hence every \(\rho_s\), is mutually absolutely continuous with \(\mu\).  If \(v=(v_0,v_1,v_2)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(q_v(u)=v_0+v_1u+v_2u^2\), then
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}H_sv=\int q_v(u)^2d\rho_s(u).
\]
Mutual absolute continuity makes the null space of this quadratic form identical for every \(s\).  Thus all \(H_s\) have the same range; because a sum of positive-semidefinite matrices has null space equal to the intersection of their null spaces, \(H_\Sigma\) has that same range.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}generalized\text{-}schur\text{-}range}\) with \(A=H_s\) and \(B=H_\Sigma\) produces \(t_s\) such that \(R_s\succeq0\) for every \(s\).  This proves \(\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing\).

Conversely, let \((m,a,b)\in\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}open\text{-}stieltjes\text{-}quartic}\), for each \(s\) there is a finite nonnegative measure \(\rho_s\) on \((0,\infty)\) with moments \(m_{s,0},\ldots,m_{s,4}\).  Set
\[
 d\nu_s(u)=D_c(u)d\rho_s(u).
\]
This is finite because \(D_c\) is a degree-four polynomial and the moments through degree four are finite.  To find its total mass, sum all sixteen cell equations in (7).  For a fixed \(s=(x,r)\), the restriction \(r_y=z\) selects exactly one \(z\) for each \(y\), and the response probabilities obey \(\sum_w p_{r_y}(w,u)=1\) and \(\sum_y p_x(y,u)=1\).  Equivalently, summing (5) over these indices yields \(D_c\).  Since \(P\in\Delta^{15}\),
\[
 1=\sum_{x,y,z,w}P(x,y,z,w)
  =\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(D_c)
  =\sum_{s\in S}\nu_s((0,\infty)). \tag{8}
\]
Thus the response measures have one probability total.  Identities (5)--(7) show that their path and APE integrals equal exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\).  The reverse implication in \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\) reconstructs one common unconditional law and legal kernels \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\).  Hence \((\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)\).

It remains to verify the strict converse.  Let \((m,a,b,t)\in\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\).  From \(R_s\succeq0\), \(\mathrm{lem{:}generalized\text{-}schur\text{-}range}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Range}(H_\Sigma)\subseteq\operatorname{Range}(H_s)
 \quad\text{for every }s. \tag{9}
\]
Because \(H_\Sigma-H_s=\sum_{j\ne s}H_j\succeq0\), one has \(\ker(H_\Sigma)\subseteq\ker(H_s)\), and symmetry therefore gives the reverse range inclusion.  The ranges in (9) are equal.  If some \(H_s=0\), (9) forces \(H_\Sigma=0\); positive semidefiniteness then forces every \(H_j=0\).  Since the entries of \(H_j\) comprise \(m_{j,0},\ldots,m_{j,4}\), every moment coordinate is then zero and the right side of (8) is zero, a contradiction.  Thus every \(m_s\ne0\).

All hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}positive\text{-}support}\) now hold.  Choose finite representing measures \(\rho_s\) on one positive-node set \(Q\subset(0,\infty)\), with every \(\rho_s\) assigning strictly positive weight to every \(q\in Q\).  Multiplication by \(D_c(q)>0\) preserves positivity of every type weight for \(\nu_s=D_c\rho_s\).  With \(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\), define the Radon--Nikodym reconstructions from \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\) nodewise.  At each \(q\in Q\),
\[
 h_x(q)=\frac{\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}{\sum_{j\in S}\nu_j(\{q\})}>0,
\]
and, for every \(x,y,z\in B\),
\[
 g_{xy}(z,q)=
 \frac{\sum_{r:r_y=z}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}{\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}>0.
\]
Both denominators are positive because every type has positive weight at every node.  Since \(\mu\) is concentrated on \(Q\), these inequalities hold \(\mu\)-almost everywhere and establish \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}initial}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}feedback}\).  Therefore the reconstructed model lies in \(\mathcal M_+(c)\), and \((\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_+(P)\).

Finally, \(m\) has \(8\cdot5=40\) coordinates and \((a,b)\) has sixteen, so the weak lift has exactly fifty-six scalar variables, eight \(3\times3\) blocks \(H_s\), and eight \(4\times4\) blocks \(K_s\).  The strict lift adds the eight coordinates of \(t\) and eight \(6\times6\) blocks \(R_s\), for sixty-four variables.  The two-sided constructions prove equality with the independently model-defined fibers, rather than an outer bound.  The cited \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\) identifies the published continuous-heterogeneity weak program and its support-grid implementation.  The equivalence proved above removes its infinite-dimensional measure quantifier without changing the weak legal models, and the common-support argument does the same for the additional strict legal restriction.  This proves the stated finite-dimensional tightening and completes both equivalences.
